tools.name: spur_search_properties
tools.title: Search properties
tools.description:
Search live listings (Zillow data) in Spur with plain English and/or structured filters, including event filters. Results show as cards and a map.

Uses 1 property-search credit per call from the user's Spur plan, or 2 credits when the search makes more than 3 ZHomes calls (e.g. several event types, tax/sale-history events, or description-based filters). To check how a sentence will be interpreted before spending a credit, call spur_parse_search_query first.

Examples:
  - "3 bed houses under $2,500/mo in Austin owned 10+ years" -> location="Austin, TX", listing_status="forRent", home_type="singleFamily", min_beds=3, max_price=2500, min_ownership_years=10
  - "duplexes for sale in 78704 built before 1980 with absentee owners" -> location="78704", listing_status="forSale", home_type="multiFamily", max_year_built=1979, only_absentee=true
  - "new pre-foreclosures or price drops of 10%+ in Dallas this week" -> location="Dallas, TX", events=["preforeclosure","price_drop"], event_within_days=7, event_min_change_pct=10
  - "motivated sellers in Houston: stale, back on market, or fired their agent" -> location="Houston, TX", events=["stale_listing","back_on_market","agent_to_fsbo"]

Events (pass in `events`; a listing matches when ANY selected event fired, and is tagged with each):
- Listing lifecycle: new_listing, coming_soon, coming_soon_active, price_drop, price_increase, pending, sold, back_on_market, delisted (automations only), open_house, rental_listed, rent_change, move_in_moved_up
- Distress & motivation: preforeclosure, foreclosure, auction, bank_owned, distress_escalated, fsbo, agent_to_fsbo, stale_listing, new_construction
- Valuation & tax: tax_assessment_posted, assessed_value_jump, tax_paid_dropped (weak), sale_recorded, zestimate_moved, equity_gap, price_below_assessed
Direct events (price_drop, pending, sold, preforeclosure, fsbo, new_listing, …) work on the first search. Change events (price_increase, back_on_market, distress_escalated, agent_to_fsbo, rent_change, zestimate_moved, …) compare against what Spur saw on an earlier search of the same area, so the first search only records a baseline.
Motivated-seller research usually combines price_drop, back_on_market, stale_listing, agent_to_fsbo and the distress stages.

Structured filters always win over what Spur infers from `query`; use query for qualitative intent (condition, style, "brick", "needs work") that only listing descriptions can match. Unset filters are left to the query.

Follow up with spur_save_properties to save listings the user likes (pass the cards' listing objects), or spur_create_search_automation to run the same filters on a schedule.

tools.name: spur_parse_search_query
tools.title: Preview search filters
tools.description:
Show how Spur interprets a plain-English property search (filters and events) without running it. Free: uses no search credit.

Use it to confirm intent before spending a credit, or to turn a vague request into explicit filters you can adjust. The returned arguments can be passed straight to spur_search_properties (keep the same location / status unless the user says otherwise). Exclusions ("no condos", "not foreclosures") are honoured by leaving those filters out.

tools.name: spur_create_workflow
tools.title: Create outreach workflow
tools.description:
Create a multi-step outreach sequence from saved templates. It's saved as an inactive draft: nothing sends until it's activated (spur_set_workflow_active) and owners are enrolled.

Send steps take a saved template: email/SMS from spur_list_message_templates (design new ones with spur_create_email_template / spur_create_sms_template), direct mail from the user's saved postcard or letter templates. Wait steps space them out. Reply/open/click branches can be added afterwards in Spur → Outreach.

Example: "text, wait 2 days, email, wait 5 days, postcard" -> steps=[{type:"send_sms",template_id:…},{type:"wait",days:2},{type:"send_email",template_id:…},{type:"wait",days:5},{type:"send_direct_mail",template_id:…}]

tools.name: spur_preview_message_draft
tools.title: Preview unsaved email or SMS
tools.description:
Preview email HTML or SMS text before saving it: renders it with sample or real owner data and runs the design checks. Nothing is saved; iterate here, then save with spur_create_email_template / spur_create_sms_template.

Email HTML guidance (see spur://email-design-guide): full HTML document, table-based layout 600px wide, inline styles on elements (a small <style> block in <head> is fine for resets/media queries), web-safe font stacks, no JavaScript, no forms, no external CSS. Images as absolute https URLs with alt text and width attributes. The user's own images (logo, headshot, property photos): spur_list_images gives their URLs; if they want to use an image they have, call spur_upload_image (or spur_save_image for a link) and use the saved URL. Use PNG or JPG in emails, not SVG. A hidden preheader <div style="display:none"> right after <body> sets the inbox snippet. Include an opt-out line ("Reply STOP" or an unsubscribe link) and the sender's postal address in the footer. Keep it under 50,000 characters. Use merge fields like {{owner_first_name}}, {{property_address}}, {{your_name}}, {{your_phone}}, {{company_name}} (see spur://merge-variables). The plain-text version is generated from the HTML unless you pass text_body.

SMS guidance: plain text, ideally one segment (160 GSM characters, or 70 if it uses emoji or other non-GSM characters; longer messages are billed per segment). Identify yourself, keep it conversational, and include opt-out wording ("Reply STOP to opt out") on first-touch messages. Links in texts from unverified numbers can be blocked, so give link-free fallback_body text when the body has a URL. Use merge fields like {{owner_first_name}}, {{property_address}}, {{your_name}} (see spur://merge-variables).

channel.description: Whether the draft is an email or an SMS

text.description: SMS text, or the email's plain-text version

fallback_body.description: SMS only: link-free text sent if links are blocked

owner_id.description: Preview with this owner's real data (spur_find_owners) instead of sample data

- From blank: start_from_blank=true gives a tested 600px responsive layout with greeting, signature and a compliant footer; pass html to replace it.
- Redesign: base_template_id copies one of the user's email templates.
- From scratch: pass html (or only text_body for a plain-text email).
The saved template can then be used by outreach workflows (spur_create_workflow / spur_set_workflow_step_template).

Email HTML guidance (see spur://email-design-guide): full HTML document, table-based layout 600px wide, inline styles on elements (a small <style> block in <head> is fine for resets/media queries), web-safe font stacks, no JavaScript, no forms, no external CSS. Images as absolute https URLs with alt text and width attributes. The user's own images (logo, headshot, property photos): spur_list_images gives their URLs; if they want to use an image they have, call spur_upload_image (or spur_save_image for a link) and use the saved URL. Use PNG or JPG in emails, not SVG. A hidden preheader <div style="display:none"> right after <body> sets the inbox snippet. Include an opt-out line ("Reply STOP" or an unsubscribe link) and the sender's postal address in the footer. Keep it under 50,000 characters. Use merge fields like {{owner_first_name}}, {{property_address}}, {{your_name}}, {{your_phone}}, {{company_name}} (see spur://merge-variables). The plain-text version is generated from the HTML unless you pass text_body.

tools.name: spur_add_postcard_qr_code
tools.title: Add QR code to postcard
tools.description:
Put a tracked QR code on the back of one of the user's postcard templates and show the preview. Each mailed postcard gets its own code under the chosen QR code, so scans are tracked per recipient (spur_get_qr_code_activity).

Placement: position="auto" fills the back's QR slot (an element with class qr-box, qr-code-box, qr-placeholder or qr-callout-box, as Spur's gallery designs have) and otherwise goes in the bottom-right of the message area, left of the address block and above the USPS barcode. Corners (top_left, top_right, bottom_left, bottom_right) and x_inches/y_inches place it in the message area; spots in the USPS clear zone are refused. Replaces any QR already on the card. If it lands on the message text, call again with another corner or move the text.

Create a QR code first with spur_create_qr_code if spur_list_qr_codes has none that fits.

position.description: Where to place the code on the back; auto fills the design's qr-box

y_inches.description: Top edge, inches from the bleed's top edge (with x_inches)

tools.name: spur_create_letter_template
tools.title: Create letter template
tools.description:
Create a letter template and show a preview. Pick the letter type first (top_first_page or insert_blank_page); it decides where the address prints and how much of the page the design can use. Three ways to start:
- From blank: start_from_blank=true gives an empty one-page letter laid out for the letter type.
- Redesign an existing template: base_template_id (yours, a Spur default or a gallery id) copies its HTML and letter type; override html or letter_type as needed.
- From scratch: pass html.

HTML guidance (see spur://letter-design-guide): one US Letter page (8.5"×11"), full HTML document with inline <style>, "@page { size: 8.5in 11in; margin: 0; }", no scripts. One root <div class="letter"> 8.5in wide; px/in units only (no vh/vw); no box-shadow, transforms or manual page breaks. top_first_page: leave the first 3.15in blank (an empty <div class="address-zone" style="height:3.15in">), body ≈ 3–4 short paragraphs. insert_blank_page: no address zone; letterhead up to 1.8in, body up to ~400 words. Images as absolute https URLs. The user's own images (logo, headshot, property photos): spur_list_images gives their URLs; if they want to use an image they have, call spur_upload_image (or spur_save_image for a link) and use the saved URL. Use merge fields such as {{owner_first_name}}, {{property_address}}, {{your_name}}, {{your_phone}}, {{company_name}} (see spur://merge-variables).

One root <div class="letter"> 8.5in wide; px/in units only (no vh/vw); no box-shadow, transforms or manual page breaks. top_first_page: leave the first 3.15in blank (an empty <div class="address-zone" style="height:3.15in">), body ≈ 3–4 short paragraphs. insert_blank_page: no address zone; letterhead up to 1.8in, body up to ~400 words. Images as absolute https URLs. The user's own images (logo, headshot, property photos): spur_list_images gives their URLs; if they want to use an image they have, call spur_upload_image (or spur_save_image for a link) and use the saved URL. Use merge fields such as {{owner_first_name}}, {{property_address}}, {{your_name}}, {{your_phone}}, {{company_name}} (see spur://merge-variables).

tools.name: spur_create_search_automation
tools.title: Create search automation
tools.description:
Schedule a recurring property search. Every run uses 1 search credit, or 2 when it makes more than 3 ZHomes calls (several event types, tax/sale-history events, furnished-only or description-based filters). New matches can be saved to a list and enriched automatically (auto_enrich spends skip-trace credits on every run, so confirm with the user).

Examples:
  - "every Monday 8am Central, Dallas rentals under $2k" -> frequency="weekly", day_of_week=1, run_time="08:00", timezone="America/Chicago", location="Dallas, TX", max_amount=2000
  - "last Friday of each month" -> frequency="monthly", day_of_week=5, week_of_month=-1
  - "every morning, new pre-foreclosures and price drops in Houston, save to my Distress list" -> frequency="daily", run_time="07:00", location="Houston, TX", events=["preforeclosure","price_drop"], list_id=…

Accepts the same advanced and event filters as spur_search_properties (min_amount / max_amount instead of min_price / max_price). Run the search once with spur_search_properties first so the user can check the results before scheduling.

In automations each event fires once, on the run that first sees it, so the same property isn't saved twice; change events start reporting from the second run. "delisted" is only available here.

Events (pass in `events`; a listing matches when ANY selected event fired, and is tagged with each):
- Listing lifecycle: new_listing, coming_soon, coming_soon_active, price_drop, price_increase, pending, sold, back_on_market, delisted (automations only), open_house, rental_listed, rent_change, move_in_moved_up
- Distress & motivation: preforeclosure, foreclosure, auction, bank_owned, distress_escalated, fsbo, agent_to_fsbo, stale_listing, new_construction
- Valuation & tax: tax_assessment_posted, assessed_value_jump, tax_paid_dropped (weak), sale_recorded, zestimate_moved, equity_gap, price_below_assessed
Direct events (price_drop, pending, sold, preforeclosure, fsbo, new_listing, …) work on the first search. Change events (price_increase, back_on_market, distress_escalated, agent_to_fsbo, rent_change, zestimate_moved, …) compare against what Spur saw on an earlier search of the same area, so the first search only records a baseline.
Motivated-seller research usually combines price_drop, back_on_market, stale_listing, agent_to_fsbo and the distress stages.
